rationale: Evidence from the iteration 0 race and its 60 trials: every run ended off_track (0 finishes). Progress was only 0.04 to 0.115, max_error reached about 0.061 (just past the 0.06 m limit), and each run had exactly one line-loss event. Steering_oscillation was low (about 0.07), so the robot was not jittering. It was drifting off the line in one swing, early in the course. The likeliest cause is that kp 2.0 with kd 0.05 gives too little damping at 1.6 base_speed, so the robot overshoots a bend or the start, loses the line once, and then goes off. Line loss is not a sensor-coverage problem in the first trial, since the sensors reach about 4.6 cm either side and the tape is 2.5 cm wide. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.6 to 1.2, to cut the momentum that carries the robot past the line; (2) kd 0.05 to 0.2, to damp the overshoot; (3) kp 2.0 to 1.5, to reduce the turn gain that may be causing the swing, while keeping enough authority for bends; (4) sensor outer x values moved from plus or minus 0.04 to plus or minus 0.05, so the line is seen earlier when the robot drifts; (5) line_loss kept at last_direction. Expected result: fewer line-loss events, max_error below 0.05, and at least some runs completing the oval. Completion time will probably exceed 3 s at 1.2 speed, so the next race should check whether progress reaches 1 with the lower speed. Hypotheses to test: (a) the early swing is an overshoot caused by kp and speed, so reducing both removes the off-track; (b) kd 0.2 is enough damping without adding jitter; (c) the outer sensors at 0.05 catch drift before line loss. Next measurements: progress and completion per track, line_loss_events by track and location, max_error, and steering_oscillation. If progress is now above 0.5 but completion_time is near 3 s, raise base_speed in steps of 0.2 while watching max_error.
